question.problem: A $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ maps the unit circle ${x\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ from ${R}^{2}$ onto an ellipse in ${R}^{2}.$ Given that the singular values of $A$ are ${\sigma }_{1}=11$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=3\sqrt{3},$ find the length of the semi-major axis of the ellipse.
question.worked_solution:
The matrix $A$ maps the unit circle ${x\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ from ${R}^{2}$ onto the ellipse ${Ax\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ in ${R}^{2}.$

First, let's re-write the squared distance from the origin to the point $Ax$ on our ellipse, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖Ax{‖}^{2} & =(Ax)^{T}(Ax) \\  & =({x}^{T}\,{A}^{T})(Ax) \\  & ={x}^{T}\,({A}^{T}\,A)x,\end{aligned}
$$

  

where ${x}^{T}({A}^{T}A)x$ is the quadratic form with the symmetric matrix ${A}^{T}A.$ 

The maximum value of this quadratic form, when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of the matrix ${A}^{T}A.$ 

The square roots of the eigenvalues of ${A}^{T}A$ are called the *singular values* of $A.$ Since the largest singular value of $A$ is ${\sigma }_{1}=11,$ the largest eigenvalue of ${A}^{T}A$ must be ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}={11}^{2}.$ So, we obtain that

$$
{max}_{‖x‖=1}{‖Ax{‖}^{2}}={11}^{2}\,⟹\,{max}_{‖x‖=1}{‖Ax‖}=11.
$$

 

Therefore, the semi-major axis of our ellipse is ${\sigma }_{1}=11.$
